root_cause: Text.append (Text branch) and Text.append_text both do `self._spans.extend(_Span(...) for start, end, style in text._spans)`. When text is self, the generator iterates the very list that extend() is growing, so every new span is re-yielded and appended forever (infinite loop / memory blowup) on `a.append(a)` or `b.append_text(b)`.
best_solution: In rich/text.py, in BOTH Text.append (the `isinstance(text, Text)` branch) and Text.append_text, iterate a snapshot: `for start, end, style in text._spans.copy()` (tuple()/list() equally fine). Reasoning from the statement alone: 'infinite loop in append' + Text being mutable -> think self-append (`x.append(x)`); look for any loop in append that reads from the argument while writing to self (extend over a generator of text._spans). Then grep for sibling methods with the same pattern (append_text, and any other `_spans.extend(... text._spans)`) and fix all of them.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_text.py::test_append_loop_regression: `a = Text('one','blue'); a.append(a); a.plain == 'oneone'` and `b = Text('two','blue'); b.append_text(b); b.plain == 'twotwo'`. Both append and append_text must terminate on self-append; no new API or exact strings beyond plain text concatenation.
locating_signals: Title says 'append'; the linked issue #3479 (not in statement body, only its URL) describes the self-append hang. `Text.append` is the obvious method name in rich/text.py; `append_text` is NOT named anywhere and must be found as a sibling with the identical extend-over-own-spans pattern.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed (v4/v6/v7/v8 kaggle_env_pass=false). v4 (555s, 22 calls) only added a reproduce_issue.py script, no source change. v6 (366s, 14 calls) and v7 (366s, 16 calls) produced empty patches. v8 (257s, 35 calls) found the right fix for Text.append (`tuple(text._spans)`) but missed the identical bug in Text.append_text, so the hidden test's `b.append_text(b)` still loops forever and the test run hangs/times out (empty test log); it also added a stray tests/test_append_self.py.
generalizable_lesson: After fixing a bug pattern in one function, grep the file/repo for the same pattern (here `_spans.extend(` over another object's list) and fix every sibling (append vs append_text, add vs add_all, etc.); hidden regression tests often exercise all public variants. Also, for 'infinite loop in X' on a container type, test the aliasing case X(self) first: mutating a list while iterating a lazy generator over it is the classic cause, fixed by iterating a copy.
